summary.one_liner: NLSOM is a Python/Streamlit framework where groups of LLMs, neural-network experts, APIs and role-players communicate in natural language, recommend and load agent "communities" for a task, and reward agents for their contributions.
summary.what_it_does: The project is the technical extension of a position paper on Natural Language-Based Societies of Mind. Given a user objective, it autonomously recommends relevant agent communities (such as vqa, search, role-play, image_colorization, image_captioning, text_to_video) and loads their agents. The agents then run a "Mindstorm" process in which they answer and interview each other before a review step checks whether the objective is solved and a summary is produced. A rough reward mechanism scores each agent by its contribution to the task. The README says the repo has 16 communities and 34 agents and is driven through a Streamlit app (app.py) that accepts text, image, audio and video inputs. The demos show visual question answering, multi-source search over arXiv, Wolfram Alpha, Wikipedia and Bing, a role-play example, and a colorize-caption-to-video chain.
use_cases: multimodal visual question answering with several models
combining search sources (arXiv, Wikipedia, Bing, WolframAlpha) for a research question
chaining image colorization, captioning and text-to-video
experimenting with multi-agent LLM collaboration and reward schemes
research prototype for society-of-mind style agent orchestration
how_to_run: conda env create -n nlsom -f nlsom.yaml (alternative to the steps above)
pip install -r requirements.txt (pip route, after creating the env)
Fill API keys in .env.template (OpenAI key is mandatory), then mv .env.template .env
notable: Mindstorm: agents interview each other in natural language to reach an answer, rather than one model handling a fixed function
Self-organizing recommendation of communities and agents from a user's natural-language goal
Per-agent reward scores recorded after each task to rate which models are useful
Modular template design so new communities and agents can be added
Accepted to CVMJ 2025 and won a Best Paper Award at the NeurIPS 2023 Ro-FoMo workshop, per the README
caveats: Install is heavy and fiddly: pinned old versions (Python 3.8, PyTorch 1.10.1, LangChain 0.0.158), manual validators build, TTS flagged as 'not recommended due to environmental conflicts'
Requires API keys (OpenAI mandatory) and manual edits to transformers and modelscope cache paths for custom checkpoint directories
Reward mechanism is described by the authors as 'albeit rough', and the v1.0 hardcoded version is distinct from the v2.0 self-organized version; v3.0 features (RL, self-improvement) are future work
keywords: combine several ai tools for one task
